newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Dec 3.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Following last night's decision by Kensington and Chelsea Conservative Association to vote to deselect Sir Nicholas Scott from his safe seat, the hunt is now on to replace him. Joan Hanham, leader of the council has been tipped as front-runner. Sir Nicholas faces a future outside politics.
ERNST & YOUNG LIFTS VEIL ON PAY SECRETS

Britain's fourth largest accountancy company Ernst & Young today released public company-style accounts for public scrutiny. The decision which has revealed that its partners earn on average 200,000 stg is only the second such action taken by one of the "big six' partnerships.

A new air alliance to rival that of BA, American Airlines and Qantas has been made by Air New Zealand, Australia's Ansett Airlines and United Airlines, who are set to co-operate on routes from the U.S. to Australia.

SOARING STERLING PUTS THE HEAT ON OVERSEAS EARNERS The increase in value of sterling has begun to affect British boardrooms and investors. Amongst those companies whose prospects have been dimmed by the surging pound are industrial materials group Cookson and BTP, specialty chemicals group.
Tension is high on the London Metal Exchange, as dealers holding options on December forward contracts must declare whether they intend to exercise those options tomorrow.
